Inside the shadowy world of anti-Putin sabotage from within Russia
- Published
Two Russian men secretly working for Ukraine's intelligence services have given rare accounts of operations they claim to have been involved with, that have targeted military assets and personnel inside Russia.
One of the men, whom we are calling Ivan, claims to have played a role from Russia in Ukrainian drone attacks on strategic bombers and munitions factories on his home soil.
He features in a BBC World Service documentary about the shadowy world of Russian saboteurs.

articles.title_original: Major fire at Canada military base leaves four dead, dozens injured
articles.title_zh: Major fire at Canada military base leaves four dead, dozens injured
facts_zh:
Major fire at Canada military base leaves four dead, dozens injured
- Published
Four members of the Canadian military have died and dozens were injured in a major fire at a base in the province of Alberta.
Addressing the nation on Sunday from Ottawa, Prime Minister Mark Carney described it as "one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime".
The fire broke out at about 16:00 local time (22:00 GMT) on Saturday at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, one of the country's busiest military training bases, and is now contained.

'Very upsetting': Residents in shock after historic French town hall set alight
A historic town hall in the French city of Limoges has been damaged in an apparent arson attack following a day of nationwide protests on Saturday.
Dramatic footage shared online shows the 19th-century building engulfed in flames, with the spire of its clock tower later collapsing.
On Sunday, stunned residents watched as firefighters, who had battled the blaze through the night, assessed the building's structural integrity.

articles.title_original: Macron calls for 'calm and order' after riots across France
articles.title_zh: Macron calls for 'calm and order' after riots across France
facts_zh:
Macron calls for 'calm and order' after riots across France
- Published
French President Emmanuel Macron has called for "calm and order" after a major day of protests turned into rioting and looting on Saturday, and as some disorder continued in Paris on Sunday.

In a national address from the Élysée Palace, he warned those who had taken part not to "escalate", adding: "We all feel anger and shame."
Some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for largely peaceful protests against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.
Macron said a distinction must be drawn between the "legitimate demands" of protesters and "those who destroyed, smashed and looted".

all_titles.en: Macron calls for 'calm and order' after riots across France

Cindy Crawford 'beyond heartbroken' after death of son Presley at 27
- Published
Supermodel Cindy Crawford has said she and her family are "beyond heartbroken" over the death of her son Presley Gerber.
"He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever," she posted on Instagram, next to a black-and-white photo of him.

"We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability."
The 27-year-old died on 20 September at a rehab facility in California.

articles.title_zh: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
facts_zh:
Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg
- Published
At least one person has been killed in an overnight attack on St Petersburg that successfully targeted two of the city's oil facilities.
The region's Governor Alexander Beglov said fires were being extinguished at the St Petersburg Oil Terminal and the Ruchyi oil depot following the attack, which also injured at least five.
A logistics centre belonging to Ozon - known as Russia's Amazon - and a data centre belonging to Facebook equivalent VKontakte were also hit.

all_titles.en: Oil facilities hit in deadly overnight attack on St Petersburg

articles.title_original: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather
articles.title_zh: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather
facts_zh:
Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather
- Published
A search for the wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane on a remote island in the Pacific Ocean has resumed after severe weather caused researchers to stop for several days.

A team has travelled to Nikumaroro Island, part of Kiribati, hoping to solve the mystery of the famed aviator's disappearance by investigating the so-called Taraia Object, spotted in the atoll's lagoon in aerial imagery.
The American pioneer vanished while attempting to circumnavigate the globe in 1937, spawning decades of speculation about her fate.

all_titles.en: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather
